title_en: Siwei Industrial (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. and Siwei Enterprise Co., Ltd. v. Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd., Avery (Kunshan) Co., Ltd., Avery (China) Co., Ltd., Nanhai Lishui Yili Printing Factory, and Foshan Huanshi Town Dongsheng Fenjiang Printing Factory Business Department — dispute over infringement of trade secrets (objection to jurisdiction)
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Article 10 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, selling infringing products manufactured through misappropriation of trade secrets does not constitute an act of misappropriation of trade secrets as defined by that Law.

full_text_en:
Siwei Industry (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. and Siwei Enterprise Co., Ltd. v. Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd., Avery (Kunshan) Co., Ltd., Avery (China) Co., Ltd., Nanhai Lishui Yili Printing Factory, and Foshan Huanshi Town Dongsheng Fenjiang Printing Factory Business Department — dispute over jurisdiction objection in a trade secret infringement case

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Article 10 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, the sale of infringing products manufactured through misappropriation of trade secrets does not constitute an act of trade secret infringement as defined under that Law.

Typically, the process of using a trade secret is the process of manufacturing infringing products. When the infringing product is completed, the infringing result of using the trade secret occurs simultaneously. Therefore, the place where the act of using the trade secret is performed and the place where the result occurs usually coincide, and it is inappropriate to regard the place of sale of infringing products as the place where the infringing result of using the trade secret occurs.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2007) Min San Zhong Zi No. 10

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Avery Dennison Corporation, domiciled at 150 North Orange Grove Boulevard, Pasadena, CA 91103, USA.
Legal Representative: Robert G. van Schoonenberg, Senior Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wei Qingsong, Attorney at Shanghai Huiye Law Firm.

Legal Representative: Robert G. van Schoonenberg, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Chen Wei, Patent Agent of Guangzhou Yuegao Patent Agency Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem: Wei Qingsong, Attorney at Shanghai Huiye Law Firm.

Legal Representative: Robert G. van Schoonenberg, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Chen Wei, Patent Agent of Guangzhou Yuegao Patent Agency Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem: Wei Qingsong, Attorney at Shanghai Huiye Law Firm.

Legal Representative: Robert G. van Schoonenberg, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Chen Wei, Patent Agent of Guangzhou Yuegao Patent Agency Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem: Wei Qingsong, Attorney at Shanghai Huiye Law Firm.

Appellees (Plaintiffs at First Instance): Siwei Enterprise Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 12, Lane 61, Section 1, Guangfu Road, Sanchong City, Taipei County, Taiwan Region.
Legal Representative: Yang Binyan, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yang Xiaoyan, Attorney at Beijing Xinrui Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhou Jian, Attorney at Guangdong Shendadi Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Siwei Industry (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Buildings 1 and 2, Fenghuang Third Industrial Zone, Fuyong Town, Bao'an District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Yang Weimeng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yang Xiaoyan, Attorney at Beijing Xinrui Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhou Jian, Attorney at Guangdong Shendadi Law Firm.

Defendants at First Instance: Nanhai Lishui Yili Printing Factory, domiciled at Shachong Shangxiangtian Industrial Zone, Lishui Town, Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Zhou Ping.

Defendant at First Instance: Foshan Huanshi Town Dongsheng Fenjiang Printing Factory Business Department, domiciled at Dongsheng Management District, Huanshi Town, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.
Responsible Person: Li Ju.

The appellants Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Avery Guangzhou Company), Avery (Kunshan) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Avery Kunshan Company), and Avery (China) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Avery China Company), dissatisfied with the civil ruling (2005) Yue Gao Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 1-1 of the Guangdong High People's Court in the case concerning the dispute over jurisdiction objection in a trade secret infringement case with the appellees Siwei Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Siwei Company), Siwei Industry (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Siwei Shenzhen Company), and the defendants at first instance Nanhai Lishui Yili Printing Factory (hereinafter referred to as Lishui Printing Factory) and Foshan Huanshi Town Dongsheng Fenjiang Printing Factory Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Fenjiang Business Department), appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and heard the case in a closed session. Chen Wei and Wei Qingsong, agents ad litem of Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery Guangzhou Company, Avery Kunshan Company, and Avery China Company, and Yang Xiaoyan and Zhou Jian, agents ad litem of Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company, appeared in court. The case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found that on April 8, 2004, Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company filed a lawsuit with the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province against Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery Guangzhou Company, Avery Kunshan Company, Avery China Company, Lishui Printing Factory, and Fenjiang Business Department for infringement of their trade secrets, including technical information on emulsified acrylic pressure-sensitive adhesive with added tackifier and business information, seeking compensation for economic losses of RMB 60 million. On May 17, 2004, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court issued a notice of case acceptance and a notice of response. On November 29, 2004, Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company submitted a "Petition for Change of Claims" to the Foshan Intermediate People's Court, changing the compensation claim to RMB 105 million. On April 8, 2005, Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company submitted another "Petition for Further Increase of Subject Matter of Action" to the Foshan Intermediate People's Court, changing the compensation claim to RMB 150 million. The Foshan Intermediate People's Court sought instructions from the Guangdong High People's Court, requesting that the case be transferred to the Guangdong High People's Court, which was approved. On June 6, 2005, Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company submitted a supplementary "Civil Complaint" to the Guangdong High People's Court.

Separately, the civil ruling (2004) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 003 of the Jiangsu High People's Court dated November 8, 2005 recorded that Avery Dennison Corporation and Avery China Company had filed a lawsuit with the Jiangsu High People's Court against Siwei Company, Siwei Shenzhen Company, Shanghai Siwei Enterprise Co., Ltd., et al. for infringement of their trade secrets, including technical information on pressure-sensitive adhesive and business information, and the Jiangsu High People's Court accepted the case on October 13, 2004. The Jiangsu High People's Court ruled that the case should be transferred to the Guangdong High People's Court on the grounds that the case and the present case were disputes arising from the same legal facts, and the Foshan Intermediate People's Court had accepted the case earlier than the Jiangsu High People's Court, and due to the transfer for jurisdictional level reasons to the Guangdong High People's Court.

According to the complaint of Siwei Company, Siwei Company believed that the "technical information on emulsified acrylic pressure-sensitive adhesive with added tackifier" it claimed was later patented by Avery Dennison Corporation in China as "tackified emulsion pressure-sensitive adhesive". Therefore, the technical secrets in dispute between Siwei Company et al. and Avery Dennison Corporation et al. were both pressure-sensitive adhesive technology.

During the period for filing a defense at first instance, Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery Guangzhou Company, Avery Kunshan Company, and Avery China Company raised a jurisdiction objection with the Guangdong High People's Court. The main reasons were: 1. Transferring this case to the Jiangsu High People's Court for trial could effectively prevent the malicious lawsuit of Siwei Company et al. 2. Since the Foshan Intermediate People's Court had no jurisdiction over this case, and the Guangdong High People's Court accepted the case later than the Jiangsu High People's Court accepted the related case, this case should be transferred to the Jiangsu High People's Court for trial.

The court of first instance held that: Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law provides that lawsuits arising from tortious acts shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or where the defendant is domiciled. Paragraph 3 of Article 22 provides that where the domiciles or habitual residences of several defendants in the same lawsuit are within the jurisdiction of two or more people's courts, each of those people's courts shall have jurisdiction. This case is a dispute over trade secret infringement. The domicile of defendant Avery Guangzhou Company is in Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province; the domiciles of defendants Avery Kunshan Company and Avery China Company are in Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province; the domiciles of defendants Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department are in Foshan City, Guangdong Province. Therefore, the people's courts of the above defendants' domiciles all have territorial jurisdiction. Since some defendants are domiciled in Foshan City, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court's acceptance of this case complies with the law. Moreover, due to the large subject matter in dispute, in accordance with relevant provisions on jurisdictional level, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court transferred this case to the Guangdong High People's Court for trial. Therefore, the Guangdong High People's Court has jurisdiction over this case according to law.

Although Avery Dennison Corporation and Avery China Company filed a lawsuit with the Jiangsu High People's Court against Siwei Company et al. for trade secret infringement, and the Jiangsu High People's Court accepted that case on October 13, 2004, the acceptance date of that case is later than the acceptance date of this case by the Foshan Intermediate People's Court, i.e., May 17, 2004. Although the Guangdong High People's Court accepted the transfer from the Foshan Intermediate People's Court in June 2005, this is merely a change in jurisdictional level, not two independent filings. Therefore, the acceptance date of this case should still be May 17, 2004. Pursuant to Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, where a lawsuit is within the jurisdiction of two or more people's courts, the court that first dockets the case shall not transfer the case to another court with jurisdiction. Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Strictly Implementing the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in Economic Trials provides that where a dispute arises between parties based on the same legal relationship or the same legal facts, and separate lawsuits are filed with different claims in different courts that have jurisdiction, the court that dockets the case later shall, within seven days after learning that another court has docketed the case earlier, rule to transfer the case to the court that first docketed the case for consolidated trial. Moreover, the Jiangsu High People's Court has already made a civil ruling (2004) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 003 according to that provision, transferring the case of Avery Dennison Corporation et al. v. Siwei Company, Siwei Shenzhen Company, et al. concerning trade secret infringement to the Guangdong High People's Court. Under these circumstances, the request of Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery Guangzhou Company, Avery Kunshan Company, and Avery China Company to transfer this case to the Jiangsu High People's Court lacks sufficient basis. In accordance with Article 22, Article 29, and Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled to dismiss the jurisdiction objections of Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery China Company, Avery Guangzhou Company, and Avery Kunshan Company.

The appellants Avery Dennison Corporation, Avery Guangzhou Company, Avery Kunshan Company, and Avery China Company appealed, stating: 1. According to the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the act of trade secret infringement does not include the conduct of sellers of infringing products. Moreover, in the complaint of Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company, only in the "Claims" section did they request Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department to cease selling infringing products; the "Facts and Reasons" section did not contain allegations against those two defendants at first instance. Therefore, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court has no jurisdiction over this case. The Guangdong High People's Court accepted the case in June 2005, which is later than the acceptance date of the related case by the Jiangsu High People's Court. According to law, this case should be transferred to the Jiangsu High People's Court for jurisdiction. 2. Transferring this case to the Jiangsu High People's Court for jurisdiction can effectively prevent Siwei Company's malicious lawsuit scheme. Siwei Company had sued Avery Dennison Corporation et al. in the Jiangsu High People's Court in 1999 and withdrew the lawsuit in 2003. In 2004, Siwei Company sued again in the Foshan Intermediate People's Court. If Siwei Company's groundless and baseless repetitive lawsuits are not stopped, it will prevent Avery Dennison Corporation et al. from conducting business activities and will inevitably waste China's limited judicial resources. Accordingly, they requested this Court to set aside the ruling of the court of first instance and designate the Jiangsu High People's Court to hear this case.

The appellees Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company argued in response: 1. Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department not only sold infringing products but also used infringing equipment and processes for slitting and sheet cutting, etc. Therefore, Foshan City is both the place where the infringing acts were committed and the place where the infringing results occurred. According to the Civil Procedure Law and its judicial interpretations, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court has jurisdiction over this case. Since the Foshan Intermediate People's Court transferred the case to the Guangdong High People's Court due to jurisdictional level, the acceptance date of this case should be the date of acceptance by the Foshan Intermediate People's Court. The Jiangsu High People's Court, based on the earlier acceptance by the Foshan Intermediate People's Court, ruled to transfer the related case to the Guangdong High People's Court for trial, which complies with the law. 2. The jurisdiction objection dispute is a procedural matter; the issue of malicious lawsuit raised by Avery Dennison Corporation et al. is irrelevant to this appeal.

This Court, upon further trial, confirms that the facts found by the court of first instance are true.

This Court additionally finds that in the complaint submitted by Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company to the Foshan Intermediate People's Court on April 8, 2004, the contents concerning Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department were: requesting the court to order Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department to immediately cease selling and using infringing products manufactured by misappropriating the plaintiffs' trade secrets. Avery Dennison Corporation et al. used the plaintiffs' trade secrets to produce, manufacture, and sell related infringing products and sold them throughout China, including Foshan City.

In the supplementary complaint submitted by Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company to the Guangdong High People's Court on June 6, 2005, the contents concerning Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department were: requesting the court to order Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department to immediately cease selling infringing products manufactured by misappropriating the plaintiffs' trade secrets. The sellers of related infringing products included Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department in Foshan City.

Both the appellants and appellees confirmed that this case and the case (2004) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 003 accepted by the Jiangsu High People's Court are disputes arising from the same legal facts between the parties.

This Court holds that although Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company alleged in the complaint that Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department sold infringing products manufactured by misappropriating the plaintiffs' trade secrets, pursuant to Article 10 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the sale of infringing products manufactured through misappropriation of trade secrets does not constitute an act of trade secret infringement as listed in that Law. Therefore, the alleged act of selling infringing products manufactured by misappropriating trade secrets by Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department is not an act of trade secret infringement under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Consequently, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court cannot acquire jurisdiction over this case based on the alleged sale of infringing products by Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department. Generally, the place where the act of using a trade secret is committed and the place where the result occurs coincide. That is, the process of using a trade secret is typically the process of manufacturing infringing products; when the infringing product is completed, the infringing result of using the trade secret occurs simultaneously, and it is inappropriate to regard the place of sale of infringing products as the place where the infringing result of using the trade secret occurs. Therefore, although Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company alleged that the appellant Avery Dennison Corporation et al. sold the allegedly infringing products into Foshan City, Foshan City is not the place where the infringing result of the appellant Avery Dennison Corporation et al.'s act of using trade secrets occurred, and the Foshan Intermediate People's Court cannot acquire jurisdiction over this case on that basis either. As for the allegation by Siwei Company and Siwei Shenzhen Company that Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department used infringing products manufactured by misappropriating the plaintiffs' trade secrets, since that act does not constitute an act of trade secret infringement under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, it cannot serve as a basis for the Foshan Intermediate People's Court to have jurisdiction over this case. As for the statement in the appellees' defense at second instance that Lishui Printing Factory and Fenjiang Business Department used infringing equipment and processes for slitting and sheet cutting, etc., since the complaint contains no such allegations and the appellees did not submit preliminary evidence to prove it, it likewise cannot serve as a basis for the Foshan Intermediate People's Court to have jurisdiction over this case.

Therefore, according to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and its judicial interpretations, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court has no jurisdiction over this case, and the Guangdong High People's Court has jurisdiction over this case. However, since this case and the case (2004) Su Min San Chu Zi No. 003 accepted by the Jiangsu High People's Court are disputes arising from the same legal facts between the parties, and the filing date of the Jiangsu High People's Court is earlier than the filing date of the Guangdong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Strictly Implementing the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in Economic Trials, this case should be transferred to the Jiangsu High People's Court for consolidated trial. The court of first instance erred in its determination of jurisdiction over this case, which should be corrected.

As for the issue of malicious lawsuit raised by the appellants, since it is irrelevant to the jurisdiction objection, this Court will not address it.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 29 and Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2005) Yue Gao Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 1-1 of the Guangdong High People's Court is set aside;

2. This case is transferred to the Jiangsu High People's Court for handling.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang
Judge: Xi Zhonglin
Acting Judge: Li Jian
January 15, 2009
Clerk: Wang Xin
